objective: Maintain a running maximum over nonempty numeric data without assuming a nonnegative seed.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Comparison-based aggregation is an enduring supported operation.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Maximum selection is useful for measurements and ranking inputs.
relevanceRationale.transferable: The running-best invariant transfers to other reductions.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Nonempty finite inputs and negative/fractional cases match the intended foundation level.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Correct initialization avoids a common numerical correctness error.

defects: The original unrestricted-size brief recommended argument spread without naming its engine limits.
Input preservation is a newly explicit policy; in-place sorting was not forbidden by the old brief.
The signed-zero tie policy was unspecified.
rationale: The revised brief bounds the array to 1–10,000 finite elements, states read-only input and accepts either zero sign as the same numerical maximum. The actual worker accepts spread, a loop, reduce, an independent -Infinity-seeded scan and copy-then-sort. Frozen negatives, unchanged order, numerical zero ties and 10,000 inputs are checked. A slower valid copy-sort is accepted for correctness; its uncertain complexity remains unpenalized.
